scale_union: Reciprocal-rank fusion (constant 60) of exact W255/k9 and W1024/k13 half-stride top-100 lists, then one C=1/10/100 budget.
verification: Exact W255/k9 and W1024/k13 half-stride top-100 candidates; best-Jaccard window pair; global edit distance <= floor(0.30W), either strand; no backfill.
uncertainty: 95% percentile bootstrap, 2000 split-group resamples, seed 568; pair-weighted recall, query work counted once.
role_of_secondary_arms: Frozen descriptive controls; no held-out retuning or choosing a new winner from them.
resource_scope: Same fixed target universe on one c7i.4xlarge; report hot query time, cold stage sums, stage work and index bytes separately. No genome-scale extrapolation from hot time.
decision: No LSH setting passing the prespecified development recall/decoy gate improves the measured recall-query-time frontier against exact full-set controls; all also add cold preparation cost. Stop the indexed selector path if this limiting-stage result survives the frozen held-out checks. Retain a separate statement for exhaustive MinHash scanning, whose highest-recall W255 arm has a small warm-time tradeoff but no cold-cost gain.
selection_reason: W255/k9/half-stride maximizes development recall among the coarse unmasked representations. W1024/k13 provides a faster contrast. Keep all geometry/masking/whole-context and fast exact controls listed above fixed. Use 512 hashes to test the strongest sampled sketch, row-2 LSH for the best high-recall selective index at W255, and row-1/row-2 LSH at W1024 to separate index recall from selectivity. W255 row-1 LSH is omitted on heldout because it exactly matches the scan rankings on development by construction and takes 350 seconds versus 11.74 seconds for scanning.
